## Context / Problem
RP-04 S7.3.a (`insincere-illogical-antlion`, 6633-219e-988a-42f6) records `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py` in its file impact because two legacy ambient config reads live there. RP-02 S2 (`brainy-cooked-hog`) MOVES both of them into the new `binding_lifecycle.py` owner, because they are lifecycle-policy config:

- `_env_int` — the defensive `os.environ.get` int parser (registry rationale cites `binding_store.py` L110; the line has already shifted once, to L109, from the RP-02 S1 T2 delegation)
- the `RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE` read that feeds the absence/retirement grace (registry rationale cites L538)

After the S2 move, S7.3.a's recorded target file no longer contains the reads it is meant to cut to the operation-snapshot seam.

## Why this needs its own ticket
The RP-02 <-> RP-04 coupling is deliberately recorded as a soft `relates_to` rather than a `depends_on`, so nothing enforces the retarget: RP-04 will silently miss the moved reads. This ticket is the durable artifact that prevents that.

`scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.py` keys `LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS` on PATH + SYMBOL (rows are `(relpath, symbol, rationale)`; line numbers appear only inside the human-readable rationale text). There are TWO entries for `binding_store.py` — one for `os.environ.get` and one for `RECONCILE R_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE` — so a path change makes both unregistered. RP-02 S2 re-registers them under `binding_lifecycle.py` in the same change so `make lint` stays green, but re-registering a moved legacy read is NOT resolving it: the read stays ambient, with byte-identical sourcing, defensive parse, default 3 and clamp minimum 1. Cutting it to the configuration seam remains RP-04 S7.3.a's slice.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] RP-04 S7.3.a's file impact names `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_lifecycle.py` instead of (or in addition to) `binding_store.py` for these reads, and names the `_env_int` and `RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE` symbols explicitly so the target cannot be missed.
- [ ] Both `config_ownership_exceptions.py` legacy entries are confirmed to sit on the post-RP-02 path, with no stale `binding_store.py` row left implying a read that is no longer there.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_config_ownership.py` passes before and after the retarget.
- [ ] The retarget does not itself change sourcing behavior — it is bookkeeping, so the seam cut stays RP-04's work.
compiled_state.title: Retarget RP-04 S7.3.a config reads to binding_lifecycle.py after RP-02 S2
